thread:
beth-sales: Prospect CISO wants a plain-English IR timeline for the POC and asks if we can "guarantee" breach notification within 72h. Also asking whether that changes pricing for Dedicated/Private. Need one-paragraph runbook + SOW blurb to drop in email.

sam-sec: Short answer: we have an IR program (detect -> triage -> contain -> eradicate -> recover -> notify -> postmortem). For hosted, we aim to acknowledge high-sev incidents within 4h, take containment steps within 24h, and provide an initial incident summary within 72h where required by law. Windows may vary by region/legal role.

ulia-oncall: For POC we can enable additional telemetry and a dedicated trace for their sessions. Quick forensic export we run:```
redwoodctl export-logs --customer-id <ID> --since 24h --out poc_forensics.tar.gz
```
We can snapshot KV caches and model state on request.

beth-sales: @dpo-liz can we promise 72h in writing?

dpo-liz: Don't promise a global 72h. Under GDPR controllers must notify authorities within 72h of becoming aware; as a processor (hosted) our obligation is to notify the customer so they can meet controller duties. Recommended contract language instead of an absolute promise.

dpo-liz: Suggested SOW blurb: "Redwood will acknowledge potential security incidents affecting the customer's environment within four (4) hours of detection and will provide an initial incident summary within seventy-two (72) hours, where legally required. Specific notification obligations for regulated personal data shall be governed by the applicable customer agreement and law."

mike-finance: Pricing: standard IR support included for Hosted. Dedicated/Private include baseline enterprise support (IR coordination hours). For an SLA-backed notification guarantee or dedicated IR retainer, we quote separately; typical retainers range $10k-$50k depending on scope.

sam-sec: Add POC checklist for buyer: 1) enable 90d logging retention; 2) RBAC + session recording for testers; 3) provide escalation list (SOC oncall, sec lead, legal); 4) confirm if they need supplier-side notification to regulators.

beth-sales: Can someone draft a 1-paragraph summary I can paste? Need it in ~30m.

sam-sec: Draft: "Redwood operates an incident response program with defined triage, containment, audit logging, and forensic artifact retention. For hosted customers Redwood will acknowledge confirmed high-severity incidents within four (4) hours and, where required by law, provide an initial incident summary within seventy-two (72) hours. Notification obligations related to regulated personal data are subject to applicable law and the terms of the customer agreement. For Dedicated and Private deployments, response and notification terms will be set in the customer-specific agreement and may include on-call or retainer services if contracted."

beth-sales: copying that into my reply. :thumbsup:
